description:
A database GUI and IDE for MongoDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, SQLite and Redis

Monghoul is a desktop database GUI and IDE for MongoDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, SQLite, and Redis with Valkey, in one window with one sidebar.

- MongoDB: autocomplete from the field names and values in your collections, an aggregation builder that runs each stage, Explain that names the index a slow query needs, schema analysis, a Database Map of the references between collections, and a cluster monitor.
- PostgreSQL: completion from your schemas and joins from your foreign keys, Explain with real rows and times, and Manual commit that holds writes in one transaction.
- ClickHouse: Explain that counts the granules a read selects, and drafts with typed parameters.
- SQLite: a database file opens with no server, and every value shows exactly as SQLite stored it.
- Redis and Valkey: a key browser on SCAN, an editor for each key type, and a command console.

On every engine, edits in the result grid are reviewed before they apply, a write that can drop data or change every row asks first, and write protection, operation logs, import and export work the same way. AI assistants connect through 77 Model Context Protocol tools, and a query that reaches a database waits for your approval.

Free to use at work. Pro adds charts, the cluster monitor, document diff, custom themes and more, with one payment.
Monghoul 2.0.2
Monghoul 2.0.2 makes it easier to start with the databases beside MongoDB. A workspace whose connections are all SQLite, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse or Redis now shows the sidebar at once. Before, the window stayed on the get-started panel until a MongoDB connection was added. A new SQLite file has no tables, and now it has a first step: Create Table in its sidebar menu opens a query tab with a draft to edit and run. On macOS, the app icon now ships in every size.
New
- Create Table on a SQLite file — A new SQLite file had no way to start a table. Its sidebar menu now has Create Table, which opens a query tab with a CREATE TABLE draft to edit and run.
Fixed
Sidebar
- The sidebar shows with only SQL or Redis connections — when every saved connection was SQLite, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse or Redis, the window stayed on the get-started panel until a MongoDB connection was added.
macOS
- The app icon in every size — the icon file now has its largest size too, so the Dock and Finder no longer scale a smaller one up.
